description: Sign-in methods, their order per platform and the sign-in screen's copy (ADR 0047, docs/SIGN_IN_SURFACES_SPEC.md §3). Every client renders this one list. The screen is also the create-account screen: a first sign-in with a method that creates accounts makes one. Flow per platform: `native` is the platform's own flow (for email and device, the client draws the form itself), `web` is a redirect through api.septena.app in the system browser sheet, `none` means the platform cannot offer it (the reason is in `notes`). The `web` platform also covers the Claude connector's authorize page. Whether a method is turned on is not the registry's job: the backend lists the methods it has on in GET /v1/auth/methods, and a client hides the others. The Terms and Privacy URLs come from plans.json `legal`.

methods.name: Apple
methods.title: Continue with Apple
methods.notes: macos is native in the App Store build. The Developer ID build has no Sign in with Apple entitlement, so the client checks at run time (SeptaskSignIn.appleAvailable) and uses the web flow there (#551). Web Apple needs the Services ID (#638).

methods.name: Google
methods.title: Continue with Google
methods.notes: android uses Credential Manager and POST /v1/auth/google/native. Clients draw Google's own mark where its branding rules ask for it; the icon is the fallback glyph.

methods.name: Microsoft
methods.title: Continue with Microsoft
methods.notes: Personal and work accounts (the common tenant). Clients draw Microsoft's own mark where its branding rules ask for it; the icon is the fallback glyph.

methods.title: Continue with email
methods.notes: A six-digit code by email (ADR 0016, #169): POST /v1/auth/email/start and /verify.

methods.title: I use Septena on another device
methods.notes: Device approval (ADR 0016): a signed-in device approves this one. It never creates an account.
